problem: Find the degree of the homogeneous function $f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}-{x}^{3}}\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{y}).$

feedback.problem: Find the degree of the homogeneous function $g(x,y)=\frac{4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}{x}\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3y}{x}).$
feedback.worked_solution:
A function $g(x,y)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
g(tx,ty)={t}^{n}g(x,y).
$$

So first, we compute $g(tx,ty),$ and then we simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}g(x,y)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(tx,ty) & =\frac{4(tx)^{2}-(ty)^{2}}{(tx)}\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3ty}{tx}) \\  & =\frac{4{t}^{2}{x}^{2}-{t}^{2}{y}^{2}}{tx}\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3ty}{tx}) \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}(4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}{tx}\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3y}{x}) \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{t}\cdot \frac{4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}{x}\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3y}{x}) \\  & =t\cdot \frac{4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}{x}\,\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{3y}{x}) \\  & =tg(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
g(tx,ty)=tg(x,y)={t}^{1}g(x,y)
$$

and so the degree of the homogeneous function $g(x,y)$ is $1.$
